(3) For a prime ℓ with r := ord_ℓ(|c|) and ord_ℓ(|G|) = r+s, and j with no proper normal subgroup of G of order divisible by ℓ^{j+1}: deg ≡ 0 mod ℓ^{⌈(r−3s−j)/2⌉}, and for nonabelian simple G not isomorphic to any PSL₂(F_q) with ℓ^{r+1} ≥ |G|^{1/3}, deg ≡ 0 mod ℓ^{⌈r/2⌉}. (4) For q ≥ 3 and any absolutely irreducible ϕ : Π → SL₂(F_q) not of dihedral type, the vertical automorphism groups of Adm(ϕ(Π))‾_ℚ‾ are reduced to {±I} and M(ϕ(Π))‾_ℚ‾ → M(1)‾_ℚ‾ is representable. (5) Genus formula: for p ∉ E_bgs the compactified coarse scheme M_p‾ of M(SL₂(F_p))^{abs}_{−2} has genus p²/12 − ((p−1)/4)Φ(p−1) − ((p+1)/4)Φ(p+1) + ε(p) with ε(p) explicit in p mod 8, genus ≥ 2 for p ≥ 13 and genus 0, 0, 1 at p = 5, 7, 11; and for a density-one set of primes M(PSL₂(F_p))^{abs}_{−2} is connected with full alternating or symmetric monodromy, hence noncongruence. Cover, in layers: admissible G-covers of prestable pointed curves with their six local conditions and the stacks Adm(G)‾ and Adm⁰(G); the reduced ramification divisor and the Higman invariant with their local constancy; the equivalence with stable marked G-curves; G-structures, the finite étale stack M(G) and the compactification M(G)‾ := Adm(G)‾ ⫽ Z(G) with its cusps; the relative dualizing sheaf on these stacks and the isomorphism σ_O*ω_{E/X} ≅ (σ*ω_{C/X})^{⊗e}; the degree theory for line bundles on 1-dimensional Deligne–Mumford stacks and the Hodge bundle of degree 1/24; the cusp analysis by normalization, gluing data, graphs and the δ-invariant with values in I(G), and the automorphism groups A_{G,u,h}; the SL₂ character variety of the free group of rank two with its trace coordinates, the identification of its F_q-points with GL₂(F_q)-classes of absolutely irreducible representations, and the resulting dictionary between components of M(G) and Aut⁺(Π)-orbits on the surfaces x²+y²+z²−xyz = t+2; the congruences for SL₂(F_q) and the genus, cusp and ramification computations for M(SL₂(F_p))^{abs}_{−2}. Every definition gets its API and the concrete acceptance cases recorded in the extraction. Import, never re-plan: prestable, stable and pointed curves from Stable reduction of curves and stable maps (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction), layer 3; generalised elliptic curves from Modular Curves PartII (ModularCurvesPartII), R13.1, and the Katz–Mazur moduli formalism and coarse curves from Modular curves, following Katz–Mazur (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves), which is existing work and is never re-planned; algebraic and Deligne–Mumford stacks, coarse spaces, rigidification and the deformation/étale-local-ring comparison from Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry), R09.4, R09.5 and R09.6; Galois categories, branch cycles, Riemann existence and Hurwitz moduli with Nielsen classes from Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups), IG.0, IG.3 and IG.5, together with permutation triples and dessins from Belyi maps, dessins d'enfants, and three-point covers (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps); tangential base points and fundamental groupoids from Anabelian geometry and nonabelian Chabauty (AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty), NC.0; the Markoff carrier — the surfaces x²+y²+z²−xyz = 0 and x²+y²+z²−3xyz = 0, the Vieta involutions, the group Γ and Markoff's theorem — from Classical arithmetic, sequences, polynomials and reciprocity (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion), CA.4, which PAPER-MARTIN-25, PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22 and this paper all source; the Markoff-modulo-p theory and strong approximation from Arithmetic dynamics, Part II: Markoff actions and strong approximation (ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIMarkoff), whose design job is pending; the Riemann–Hurwitz genus formula from Algebraic curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves), layer 7; and Faltings' theorem from Heights, rational points and obstructions (HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions), RP.4. Reuse Mathlib's Galois categories and fibre functors, FreeGroup, WeierstrassCurve.j, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup with trace, Nat.totient, and Tau Ceti's permutation triples with their Euler characteristic and covering-space monodromy; plan no second carrier for any of these. Record Conjectures 1.1.3 and 1.1.4 and Question 1.4.1 as open, and do not assert the Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak conjecture for the finitely many exceptional primes: what is proved is its truth outside an explicitly bounded finite set. Use the corrected count |f^{−1}(0)| = (deg f + 2)/3 of the finding recorded in this extraction, not the printed Proposition 5.6.1(a).

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-CHEN-24), to be respected when stating the layers:
- The factor 2 in the combinatorial congruence (Theorem 1.1.2) is gained exactly when ϕ∘γ_{−I} ≠ ϕ in Epi^ext(Π,G). The printed sentence has the condition reversed; G = S₃ with ℓ = 3 is a counterexample. The coarse degree is |O/⟨γ_{−I}⟩| for the orbit O, which is how §4 states it.
- The printed proof of Lemma 4.12.2 covers only j = 0. For j ≥ 1 it gives ℤ/ℓ^k × ℤ/ℓ^{k−2j}, so Corollary 4.12.5(a) is proved with the modulus ℓ^{⌈(r−3s−2j)/2⌉}; state (3)(a) for j = 0 or supply a proof. The simple-group case (b) and the SL₂ applications use j = 0 and are unaffected.
- The connectedness and genus statements need p ≥ 5, not just p ∉ E_bgs: for p = 2, 3 the stacks are empty.
- Tr_* : Aut(Π) → Aut(A³) is an anti-homomorphism that factors through Out(Π)/⟨γ_{−I}⟩; it is not injective.
- Theorem 5.5.9 needs ord_ℓ(q(q²−1)) = r + s, and the Meiri–Puder condition MP(p) is the order of (3+√5)/2 being at least 32√(p+1).
- Lemma 6.1.3(c),(d) need m_R to be G-stable, and Proposition 6.1.4 needs G_p̄ to act faithfully on the local ring, not just on fibres. Every use in the paper satisfies both.
- |𝔣^{−1}(0)| = (deg 𝔣 + 2)/3, as already said above.
Also import Nielsen's theorem Out(F₂) ≅ GL₂(ℤ), a new item planned here, and InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.1 for the prime-to-p fundamental group of a punctured elliptic curve.

The atlas plans abelian level structures on elliptic curves — Γ(N), Γ₁(N) and Γ₀(N) — in the Tau Ceti roadmap Modular curves, following Katz–Mazur and in Modular Curves PartII, and it plans Hurwitz moduli in general at IG.5, but nothing plans the moduli of elliptic curves with G-structures for a nonabelian finite group G, the stacks Adm(G)‾ of admissible G-covers of 1-generalized elliptic curves, their cusps and automorphism groups, or the congruence on the degree of their components over the j-line. A Part II of Modular curves was considered and rejected: the objects here are covers of elliptic curves classified by Nielsen classes rather than level structures in the Katz–Mazur sense, the base curve is M(1) rather than a modular curve, and the resulting curves are generically noncongruence, which is the opposite of that roadmap's subject; a Part II of Inverse Galois theory was also rejected because the material is moduli-of-elliptic-curves theory rather than realization theory, and because that roadmap's Part II direction is already claimed by the accepted route of PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 for homological stability.
